cues.text: This equation is MAP minus ICP.
MAP is the mean arterial pressure.
ICP, the intracranial pressure, is subtracted from it.
The difference is the cerebral perfusion pressure.
Normally, MAP is between 60 and 160 mmHg, and ICP is about 10 mmHg,
giving a CPP of 50 to 150 mmHg.
In that range, autoregulation maintains sufficient blood flow.
So if MAP falls or ICP rises, the perfusion pressure falls.
